question.problem:
Given that the function

$$
g(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\sqrt{x+1}, & x\le 8 \\ ax+2, & x>8\end{aligned}
$$

is continuous at $x=8,$ find the value of the constant $a.$
question.worked_solution:
At $x=8,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {8}^{-}}g(x) & =g(8) \\  & =\sqrt{8+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3,\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {8}^{+}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {8}^{+}}(ax+2) \\  & =8a+2.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=8,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {8}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {8}^{+}}g(x) \\ 3 & =8a+2 \\ 8a & =1 \\ a & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
